help.tips[0].en.text: kriegen (ugs.) – bekommen (neutral) – erhalten (formell) · gucken – sehen – betrachten · anfangen – beginnen (both neutral; beginnen slightly more written) · helfen (neutral) – unterstützen, Beistand leisten (formell) · sagen – mitteilen, sich äußern · brauchen – benötigen · checken – prüfen – überprüfen · klauen – stehlen – entwenden · sterben – versterben · kapieren – verstehen – nachvollziehen · hinkriegen – schaffen – bewerkstelligen.
help.tips[0].en.title: Verbs: colloquial ↔ formal
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The guy's annoyed because his job's gone. — The employee is aggrieved because his post was cut.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: That cost a load of dough. — This caused considerable costs.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: In a formal report a person is der Mitarbeiter; Typ and Kerl are colloquial and clash with the nominal style around them.
help.tips[1].en.text: Kohle, Knete (ugs.) – Geld (neutral) – Mittel, Betrag (formell) · Job – Arbeit, Stelle – Tätigkeit, Position · Typ – Mann – Person, Mitarbeiter · ’ne Menge – viele – zahlreiche, erhebliche · kaputt – defekt · sauer – verärgert, ungehalten · echt gut – ausgezeichnet · riesig – beträchtlich · blöd – unklug, töricht.
help.tips[1].en.title: Nouns and adjectives
help.tips[1].en.trap: versterben is only for people and only in formal contexts (obituaries, reports); 'der Hund ist verstorben' is comic. And erhalten replaces kriegen but not bekommen in 'Kinder bekommen' (to have children).
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The minister, it is said, had 'checked' the matter – note the quotation.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The event begins at 9 o’clock. (neutral) — We start at nine. (colloquial)
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: A sudden drop in register inside a formal text marks a quotation or irony; the writer does not adopt the phrase as their own.
help.tips[2].en.text: umgangssprachlich (kriegen, Kohle, checken): speech, chat, character voice. neutral (bekommen, Geld, prüfen, beginnen, helfen): most writing. gehoben / formell (erhalten, Mittel, überprüfen; versterben, sich begeben, gewahren): official, academic, literary. A sudden drop in level inside a formal text = irony or quotation.
help.tips[2].en.title: Three levels, and what each signals
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: require, verify, purloin (up) — need, check, nick (down)
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: genehmigen is the prefixed official verb; abnicken and durchwinken are colloquial images for approving something without much scrutiny.
help.tips[3].en.text: erhalten / benötigen / überprüfen / zahlreiche vs kriegen / brauchen / checken / 'ne Menge. If you're unsure of a word's level, its length and its prefix usually tell you.
help.tips[3].en.title: Longer, Latinate, prefixed = up; short, Germanic, particle-friendly = down
help.context.en: Chat: 'Haven't got the dough yet, the device is bust, and the support guy says he has to check first. Really annoying.' — Complaint: 'I have not yet received the amount; the device is defective, and the member of staff responsible informed me that he would first have to verify the facts. This is decidedly unsatisfactory.'
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: versterben is for people in formal register.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: One colloquial verb inside a formal sentence is the mix the raters hear first.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: Over-formal in an informal context is also a register error.
help.hookEn: Kriegen, bekommen, erhalten: learn to pick the word that fits a chat, an everyday email or an official letter.
help.introEn: Register — choosing the word that fits the situation — is what separates sounding fluent from sounding foreign, and it works by levels, not by single words. Umgangssprachlich (chat, speech, character voice): kriegen, kaputt, klauen, checken, Kohle, gucken, sauer, ’ne Menge, kapieren, hinkriegen. Neutral (most writing and speech): bekommen, Geld, prüfen, beginnen, helfen, sagen, brauchen, sterben. Gehoben / formell (official letters, reports, obituaries): erhalten, entwenden, überprüfen, benötigen, verärgert, mitteilen, betrachten, bewerkstelligen, versterben, sich äußern. The formal word is usually longer, often Latinate or prefixed (be-, ver-, er-, ent-), and goes with nominal style; the colloquial one is short, Germanic, and goes with particles and contractions. At this stage you move between the three levels on demand and hear a shift in a text as a signal (irony, quotation, character voice). Neither level is ‘better’; the wrong one in the wrong place is the error — and mixing two levels in one sentence is the error native listeners hear first. This quiz gives you the colloquial sentence and the formal frame (or the reverse); you supply the word that fits the frame.
help.rememberEn[0]: Three levels: ugs. – neutral – formell; Geld and beginnen are neutral, Mittel and erhalten are formal.
help.rememberEn[1]: Shift the whole sentence, not one word; a level drop inside a formal text is a signal.
help.recallEn.known: From "Register: informell → formell": du-chat to Sie-e-mail.
help.recallEn.today: Three levels per word (kriegen, bekommen, erhalten) and what each one signals.
sentences[3].whyEn: checken → überprüfen — plus the Konjunktiv müsse.
sentences[6].whyEn: sagen → mitteilen — separable: teilen Sie … mit.
sentences[12].whyEn: helfen → unterstützen — with the courtesy formula.
sentences[15].whyEn: The reverse: der Betrag → die Kohle — shifting the register down.
sentences[16].whyEn: äußern → gesagt — and the Konjunktiv disappears.
